Driven at 1024, 1280 and 1440 with the plan pane scrolled to 0/200/300/400/600/900/1200/max, the row the line names is ALWAYS the topmost row visible in the plan pane, at every offset and every desk width (titleOnScreen true, 15/15 samples). speak() picks the first row whose top is at or below the PANE's own edge - that is exactly what the round-7/8 fix was for, and its code comment says so. So 'the row it refers to may be anywhere in a pane that scrolls independently' is factually wrong: at pane.scrollTop 600 the line reads '22 August · 37 days away' at y547 x186 while 'Final dress fitting / Sat 22 Aug' is on the same screen at y348 x710, in 24px type, the largest thing in the pane. Prefixing the title prints that title twice on one screen ~560px apart - the identical duplication the panel refuted three times on the editor's reserved band ('filling it with the moment's name prints that name three times within 250px'). (2) The 'two counts with nothing saying so' claim is also wrong as drawn: measured, '79' (b268) is followed by 'Saturday 3 October 2026' (t413), 'Wedding day' (t456), the indigo today rule (t506) and 'TODAY IS 16 JULY' (t515) before the note (t547). Each figure is bound to its own named date inside its own line; they are not a bare stack and 146px of dated, ruled separation sits between them. (3) The lead tick. The measure is role=list with aria-label 'What is still ahead, nearest first' and seven role=listitem children; the aria snapshot confirms AT announces item 1 of 7 under that name. Item 1 of a list whose accessible name is 'nearest first' IS the next thing - the condition is named in words once, at the list, rather than repeated on every row. The lock clause cited is therefore met, and the lock's OWN narrowing is the opposite of the fix: 'the measure has no condition labels at all; what is next is a filled tick and the nearest item.' Adding ' the next thing,' reinstates the per-row condition label that narrowing retired; calling it hidden does not make it not a label. It would also pile up badly against the existing run string: '16 days away, the next thing, first of 2 moments on this day,'. The tick is 9px indigo against 7px ink, not '6px', and aria-hidden on it is correct - the rail is the picture, the words are elsewhere. (4) The fix makes it worse where it costs most. The note is capped at 344px; injected with the fixture's own titles, 2 of 7 wrap to two lines (23px -> 45px), so the pinned column would change height as the user scrolls the OTHER pane. User titles are arbitrary length, so the real rate is higher. The one thing the lock promises at desk width is 'the horizon never moves'; this makes its last line breathe on every scroll.
